rows.quote: In one of the rainiest places on Earth, I paid for water.
rows.statement: Mawsynram is one of the rainiest places on Earth: the World Meteorological Organization lists it as having the greatest average annual rainfall in its Asia region (11,872 mm, 1941–1979).

nguon.title: Greatest Average Annual Rainfall, WMO Region II (Asia)

rows.quote: The World Meteorological Organization lists Mawsynram as the record holder for average yearly rainfall in Asia. About eleven thousand eight hundred and seventy-two millimetres, averaged from nineteen forty-one to nineteen seventy-nine. That's about four hundred and sixty-seven inches.
rows.statement: The World Meteorological Organization lists Mawsynram, India, as the record for the greatest average annual rainfall in WMO Region II (Asia): 11,872 mm (467.4 inches), based on data from 1941 to 1979 (38 years of record).

nguon.title: Greatest Average Annual Rainfall, WMO Region II (Asia)

rows.quote: Left to pile up, one year of it would stand almost twelve metres deep. About thirty-nine feet. Taller than a three-storey house.
rows.statement: An average annual rainfall of 11,872 mm corresponds to a water depth of about 11.9 metres (about 39 feet), more than the height of a typical three-storey house (roughly 9–10 metres).

rows.quote: Is it the wettest place on the whole planet? Depending on who's measuring. Nearby Cherrapunji and two spots in Colombia have numbers of their own.
rows.statement: Whether Mawsynram is the wettest place on Earth is disputed: nearby Cherrapunji (Sohra) holds the WMO world record for the greatest 12-month rainfall (26,470 mm, August 1860 to July 1861) and has a comparable long-term average; Lloró and López de Micay in Colombia have reported higher average annual rainfall that the WMO has not evaluated; and in 2013 an India Meteorological Department official said it could not be concluded with certainty which place is wettest.

rows.quote: In the monsoon, warm wet air blows north off the bay, and across the plain nothing gets in its way. Then it hits this plateau. Mawsynram sits about fourteen hundred metres up, roughly forty-seven hundred feet. The air is shoved up the slope. It cools, and its water falls out.
rows.statement: During the summer monsoon, warm moist air from the Bay of Bengal flows north across the flat Bangladesh plains and is forced up the steep southern slopes of the Meghalaya plateau (Mawsynram lies at about 1,431 m, roughly 4,700 feet), where it cools and its moisture condenses into very heavy orographic rainfall.

nguon.title: Mechanism of Orographic Precipitation around the Meghalaya Plateau Associated with Intraseasonal Oscillation and the Diurnal Cycle (Sato 2013)

rows.quote: According to satellite studies of these hills, the heaviest rain tends to come between midnight and early morning.
rows.statement: Satellite-based studies (Ohsawa et al. 2001; Romatschke and Houze 2011, cited by Sato 2013) found that rainfall around the Meghalaya plateau peaks from around midnight to early morning, associated with a nocturnal low-level wind from the Bangladesh plains striking the southern slopes; hourly records at Cherrapunji (1946–1949) also showed more rain from 1 to 7 a.m. No hourly rainfall data exist for Mawsynram itself.

rows.quote: Khasi families trace their line through the mother. By custom, the youngest daughter, called ka khadduh, keeps the ancestral house and the family land. Keeps, not owns. It belongs to the whole lineage, and selling it needs the agreement of her mother's brothers and her own brothers.
rows.statement: The Khasi are matrilineal: descent is traced through the mother, and by custom the youngest daughter (ka khadduh) is the custodian, not the individual owner, of the ancestral house and family property, which belong to the lineage; selling it traditionally requires the consent of her maternal uncles and brothers.
